correctness.rationale: The spherical normal fan consists of 2F-4 triangles. Every triangle with all three sides >= pi/2 occupies at least pi/2 area by spherical cosine law and Girard. For F>=7 at most seven triangles can have this property. Every other triangle meets one short spherical edge, each incident to two triangles, giving 2F-4-2m<=7 and hence m>=F-5. For the upper bound, Li–Wang–Yu normals satisfy a strictly positive three-term recurrence and remain a simple vertex-truncation sequence; pairwise normal dot products have negative sign at index gaps 1 and 2, positive at gap 3, and negative with the bottom normal. Thus there are F-4 strictly obtuse edges and max dihedral < pi/2 + asin(4/R), with R arbitrarily large. Mpmath checker passed 12 finite witness instances (F=4..10 and 4..8), not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new part is the universal lower bound for every simple spatial polytope and the resulting sharp asymptotic one-third law. Li–Wang–Yu provides upper witnesses but not the universal lower count. Coxeter gives zero-obtuse classification, not the partial-obtuse count. The nearest accessible published-finding corpus record establishes a two-sided angular pinching facet bound under extra lower angle hypothesis, with no stated count lower bound; its full proof was not accessible. value.rationale: The paper establishing the sharp near-right dihedral facet-count threshold leaves the natural quantitative question of how many edges must cross a right angle. The theorem forces at least F-5 such edges, and the known construction, when its sign spectrum is calculated, realizes F-4, so the limiting proportion is exactly one third even under arbitrary upper pinching. This is a motivated asymptotic extremal invariant, not a routine numerical slice; fixed-F exact minima remain unresolved.
